concepts.title: Huygens Principle and Wavefront Construction
concepts.definition: A wavefront is the locus of points vibrating in step, and Huygens' construction treats every point of it as a source of secondary wavelets whose forward envelope gives the wavefront a moment later.
concepts.formula: new_front = tangent envelope of wavelets of radius v * t
concepts.key_idea: The construction rebuilds reflection and refraction geometrically: straightness of rays comes from wavefronts of constant phase.

solution_steps.action: seed wavelets on the given front
solution_steps.explain: each wavefront point launches a secondary wavelet moving at the wave speed
the common tangent of the wavelets is the wavefront at the later time

concepts.title: Speed of Light in a Medium
concepts.definition: Light moves slower inside a material than in vacuum, and the refractive index is exactly the factor by which the vacuum speed gets cut down.
concepts.key_idea: Frequency survives refraction unchanged while speed and wavelength drop together.

solution_steps.action: divide the vacuum speed by the refractive index
solution_steps.explain: n is defined as c over v, so v is the vacuum speed split by n

concepts.title: Wavelength Change on Refraction
concepts.definition: Crossing into a slower medium squeezes the wave: the wavelength scales by the ratio of the two propagation speeds while the frequency stays fixed.
concepts.key_idea: Crests are produced at a fixed rate, so a slower medium packs them closer together.

solution_steps.explain: equal travel times mean the wavelengths follow the speeds, lambda1/lambda2 = v1/v2

concepts.title: Critical Angle Between Two Media
concepts.definition: For a wave hitting the boundary with a faster medium, the critical angle is the incidence angle that would refract the ray along the surface; any steeper incidence gives total internal reflection.
concepts.key_idea: Refraction dies out beyond the critical angle, so the boundary behaves like a perfect mirror.

concepts.title: Coherent and Incoherent Addition of Waves
concepts.definition: Two beams interfere visibly only when they hold a steady phase difference; then amplitudes add and the intensity oscillates between dark and bright, while phase-jittering beams just stack their intensities.
concepts.key_idea: Coherence locks maxima and minima in place; incoherent sources wash the pattern into a flat 2 I0 average.

concepts.title: Fringe Spacing in Young's Double Slit
concepts.definition: In Young's arrangement the bright and dark bands sit at equal intervals set by the wavelength, the screen distance and the slit separation.
concepts.key_idea: Adjacent bright fringes are one lambda D over d apart, so wider slit gaps crowd the fringes together.

concepts.title: Wavelength From Fringe Measurements
concepts.definition: Measuring where an order-n bright fringe falls on the screen turns Young's experiment into a wavelength meter: the displacement carries lambda times n D over d.
concepts.key_idea: One ruler measurement of fringe position pins down the light's wavelength.

concepts.title: Single-Slit Diffraction Minima
concepts.definition: Light spread by a narrow slit of width a goes dark in directions where the width covers a whole number of wavelengths, giving minima at angles of n lambda over a.
concepts.key_idea: A wider slit squeezes the diffraction pattern toward the straight-through direction.

concepts.title: Malus Law Transmission
concepts.definition: Polarized light meeting an analyzer keeps the intensity component along the pass axis, so the transmitted beam carries I0 times the square of the axis-angle cosine; a single polaroid halves natural light first.
concepts.key_idea: Crossed polaroids kill the beam while parallel ones pass it fully, with the cosine-squared law filling the angles between.

solution_steps.explain: only the pass-axis field component survives, cutting amplitude by cos of the tilt

concepts.title: Polarisation and the Polaroid
concepts.definition: Only transverse waves can be polarised: a polaroid's aligned molecules drain the field component along them and hand on the rest, linearly polarised along the pass axis.
concepts.key_idea: Polarisation proves light is transverse, since longitudinal sound waves have nothing to filter.
